python-reading-a-traceback.svg.title: Reading a Python error from the bottom up
python-reading-a-traceback.svg.caption: The last line tells you what went wrong. The lines above show the path the program walked. Find the line from your own file, fix one thing, and run again.
steps: Red text appears. This is a clue, not a punishment.
It names the error type, like TypeError, and gives a message.
Find the nearest line of yours
Look for 'File app.py, line 5'. That is your code.
Look at the exact spot and the values involved.
print(total) shows what the value really is.
Number plus text? Missing key? Wrong name?
Fix it and run again. One change at a time.
Write down what it taught you.

python-strings-and-f-strings.svg.title: Text tools in Python
python-strings-and-f-strings.svg.caption: A string is a necklace of numbered letters. Methods like strip and split give back new strings. An f-string fills values into a sentence.
steps: word = "python" is six letters in a row.
word[0] is 'p'. word[-1] is 'n', the last.
word[0:3] is 'pyt'. It stops before the end number.
'a,b'.split(',') gives a list. '-'.join(list) glues it back.
Every method returns a NEW string. Save it in a variable.
f"Hello, {name}!" puts the value of name into the text.

python-classes-and-objects.svg.title: A cookie cutter and its cookies
python-classes-and-objects.svg.caption: A class describes what every object has and can do. Each object keeps its own data. self is how a method refers to the object it is working on.
steps: class Note: is the cookie cutter.
def __init__(self, title) runs when a new object is made.
n = Note('Math') makes one cookie from the cutter.
Inside a method, self.title is this object's title.
n.shout() runs the method. Python passes n as self.
Another Note has its own title. Changing one leaves the other.
__init__ can refuse a blank title, so bad notes cannot exist.
Use a @dataclass or a Pydantic model instead of a long class.

python-decorators-and-generators.svg.title: Wrapping paper and a vending machine
python-decorators-and-generators.svg.caption: A decorator wraps a function to add behavior. A generator uses yield to hand back one value at a time. FastAPI uses both: @app.get registers routes, and yield dependencies clean up.
steps: def add(a, b): return a + b
It does something extra, like printing, then calls the real function.
Registers the function as the handler for GET /health.
def count(): yield 1; yield 2 hands back one value at a time.
The function freezes at yield and continues later.
Open the session, yield it, then close it in finally.
Even after an error, the session is closed.

python-calling-another-api.svg.title: Your app as a careful client
python-calling-another-api.svg.caption: When your app calls another service, protect it: set a timeout, check the status, keep the API key secret, and have a safe fallback ready.
steps: The API key comes from an environment variable.
The timeout stops one slow service from freezing your app.
Return a clear 503 message, not the other service's raw error.
Send back only the fields your own API promises.
